html:
ForgeMCP 0.2.17 — Reset authorization resolution

Checked October 24, 2026. Verdict: READY FOR FRESH RESET AUTHORIZATION, with the prior refusal's exact guard predicate unconfirmed. This is a bounded read-only diagnosis. No new request, preview, terrain edit, save, Editor launch, build, checkpoint restoration, or Trello update occurred.

Refused request and native guard

The owner entered Forge.Landscape.ApproveEditSession 672FB6EC401392B74E67AF852B57A393 at 2026-10-24 06:34:50.110 UTC. The Editor log immediately returned Landscape adoption refused: request stale or unsaved/unsafe world. with a blank diagnostic suffix. Native status still finds that exact request with approved=false, revoked=false, expires_at_unix=0, no backup root, no active operation, no operation records, apply_heightmap only, ForgeTerrain GUID 2E6FC5F94C4EF704F700299B5D08C23B, and inclusive authorization region [1042,1065,1098,1075]. Preflight lists it as used=false, with no native checkpoint. The request did not create an editing grant.

Installed adapter source Plugins/Forge/Source/MajesticForge/Private/ForgeLandscapeAdoption.inl shows the pending approval window is 300 seconds after request creation (RequestExpires=UtcNow()+300, line ~286). The requested 3,600-second session lifetime starts only after approval (line ~332). The approval guard (lines ~301–308) uses a single warning for: missing/wrong-type/already-approved/revoked request; pending expiry; Editor/world/Landscape/layer/transform identity failure; Landscape readiness failure; or world/external-package dirty state. Only the readiness function fills the printed Error string. The blank suffix therefore gives no specific failure code; it is consistent with pending expiry, identity mismatch, or dirty-state rejection. Source shows no independent world-generation/revision token stored in the request. Its binding is the weak world/actor pointers, session PID, project/world/actor paths, Landscape/layer GUIDs, World Partition flag and Landscape transform.

Crucially, status/preflight expose expires_at_unix=0 and expired=false for an unapproved request because those fields describe the post-approval grant, not RequestExpires; the pending timestamp/expiry is not exposed. The native request itself does not record a creation timestamp in the inspected log or a request artifact. The reset report was created at 06:30:15 UTC, proving only that the request preceded that time. Approval at 06:34:50 UTC was at least 4 minutes 35 seconds later. A creation before 06:29:50 would make pending expiry the direct cause, but that exact creation time is unavailable. Pending expiry is the strongest timing explanation, not a confirmed sole cause. The log does not evidence a changed PID/world, a dirty package, or an unsafe component at the refusal instant. A later clean inventory/preflight cannot retroactively prove those were clean at 06:34:50.

Current identity and safety

Fresh discovery authenticates the same active unreal-33500 / PID 33500, UE 5.6.1-44394996+++UE5+Release-5.6, ForgeMCP 0.2.17-alpha.1, project [local path], level /Game/Levels/L_City_World_Master.L_City_World_Master, PIE stopped. Landscape GUID BD45FDD94EC2A29617B50794F2DE4E9D, World Partition, 16 loaded/0 unloaded proxies, 64 registered Landscape and 64 registered collision components, clean/up-to-date layers. Original Layer GUID 198824024FF8A77A01535B86021D9B34 remains full-height MD5 9f43572fbc2c06ef497da015879cdb23; ForgeTerrain full-height MD5 remains f5a8d55a3372fefe6fcadb0e7ff25b07. Fresh bounded ForgeTerrain read [1042,1065,1098,1075] returned 627 samples, 197 nonzero, MD5 0bce98df53283065e7a173d2d0c56d73, unchanged from the reset plan.

Fresh complete native loaded-package inventory inspected 1,192 packages without errors, limit hit or further page; only compiled-in /Script/SlateCore is dirty, with zero loaded production Content packages dirty. Fresh read-only editing-session preflight for the exact scoped request reports target layer ready/visible/unlocked, clean checkpoint source, readable 23-file backup scope and no current readiness blocker. This confirms current eligibility, not successful approval or the earlier failure's exact cause.

Checkpoint and original height baseline

The new pre-change checkpoint [local path] remains readable; manifest SHA-256 41ad3a15a126a4b2a3abe95ec796fa215388fc317504b20703c6d2403395baf4. All 23 listed production sources and all 23 backup copies were rehashed against the manifest with zero mismatches. Historical checkpoints were not changed or restored.

The earliest verified pre-sculpt ForgeTerrain height baseline is flat 0 local cm, full-height MD5 9f43572fbc2c06ef497da015879cdb23, established before the first authorized riverbed job in the first live sculpt report [not indexed]. It is the ForgeTerrain edit-layer baseline, not an instruction to flatten Original Layer or world elevation. The confirmed ForgeMCP regions are original riverbed [1055,1067,1085,1073], left extension [1043,1068,1057,1074], and right extension [1083,1066,1097,1072]. Current protected readback has 101+60+36 = 197 surviving negative samples in their combined rectangle; the other 24 right-extension samples were later zeroed. Two additional indentations remain of unidentified provenance and location and are outside the authorized reset definition.

Fresh authorization procedure, not executed

  1. Immediately before any new request, rediscover the sole responsive Editor and verify project, world, PID, version, Landscape/layer GUIDs, PIE stopped, all proxies/components, complete clean production Content, stable 627-sample MD5, and the 23-file source/checkpoint hashes. Stop on a changed value.
  2. For separate owner approval to initiate a single new request, use unreal_request_landscape_edit_session once with session unreal-33500 only if still current, Editor PID 33500, project [local path], world package /Game/Levels/L_City_World_Master, actor /Game/Levels/L_City_World_Master.L_City_World_Master:PersistentLevel.Landscape_UAID_701CE7E46087BA0D03_2100287295, Landscape GUID BD45FDD94EC2A29617B50794F2DE4E9D, layer_name=ForgeTerrain, layer GUID 2E6FC5F94C4EF704F700299B5D08C23B, world_partition=true, region_scope=bounded, inclusive region [1042,1065,1098,1075], action apply_heightmap only, lifetime 3,600 seconds after approval. Do not reuse 672FB6EC401392B74E67AF852B57A393.
  3. Record the new request ID and creation clock immediately. The owner must inspect the local dialog and run only its returned Forge.Landscape.ApproveEditSession <new-id> in that same Editor well within 300 seconds. If that cannot be done, do not submit a request yet. Immediately check native status for approved=true, valid session expiry, matching scope, and a created/hash-verified native backup. On refusal, denial or timeout, stop; do not retry automatically.
  4. Only after approval, take a fresh exact height read and native preview for one apply_heightmap patch of zero local-cm samples across inclusive [1043,1066,1097,1074] (55×9). Require its before array to match the current protected baseline, exactly 197 predicted negative-to-zero changes, no changes in the surrounding halo, unchanged Original Layer, and no touch to unidentified indentations. Review preview/job scope and package ownership before any separately authorized apply. Do not use a global flatten action.
  5. After a separately approved apply, verify every patch/halo sample, full-layer hashes, 16 proxies, 64/64 components and dirty-package ownership. Saving requires separate exact-package owner authorization; independent reload requires a later separate launch authorization. No save, reload or automatic rollback is part of the editing grant.

Next practical step: arrange the owner at the existing Editor so a new request, local dialog and status verification can complete inside the five-minute pending window; first repeat the short read-only identity/safety gates. The only technical uncertainty is the historical refusal's exact predicate, which the current API/log does not expose. There is no currently evidenced safety condition blocking a fresh exact-scoped request. The reset itself remains unperformed.
